title: GitHub - Xafloc/ahp-matrix: Modern AHP decision matrix: pairwise comparisons, consistency checks, sensitivity analysis — single binary with a web UI
excerpt: Modern AHP decision matrix: pairwise comparisons, consistency checks, sensitivity analysis — single binary with a web UI - Xafloc/ahp-matrix
content_html:
Make better decisions with the Analytic Hierarchy Process: compare your options two at a time, check that your judgments agree with each other, and see how robust the winner is. AHP Matrix is a single binary that runs a local web app. Your projects stay on your machine as .ahp.json files.

  • Compare in pairs on a balance. Arrow keys tip it, Enter moves to the next pair, and you get useful results long before every pair is answered.
  • Rate or measure where pairs are overkill. Each criterion can be compared in pairs, rated 1–10, or given measured values such as price ("lower is better").
  • Group criteria into a hierarchy, so you only compare criteria that belong together.
  • Catch contradictions. Every set of comparisons gets a consistency ratio, and the app points out the answers that disagree with the rest, with a one-click fix.
  • Several people. Everyone judges separately, the results combine them (weighted), and the app shows where people disagree most. Send someone their own copy, then merge it back when they return it.
  • What if? Drag a criterion's weight and watch the ranking change. Each criterion shows how far it can move before the winner changes.
  • Bring your spreadsheet. Import workbooks made with the classic "Priority Matrix" Excel template, and export results to Excel or CSV.
  • Start from an example or a template, including vendor selection with the template's 23 criteria, grouped.

Install

Download the archive for your system from the latest release (macOS, Linux and Windows, Intel or ARM), unpack it, and run ahp-matrix. It starts on http://127.0.0.1:7777 and opens your browser.

On macOS, Homebrew is the easiest way:

brew install xafloc/tap/ahp-matrix

The macOS binaries aren't notarized (Homebrew takes care of that for you). If macOS blocks the one you downloaded, run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ahp-matrix once in the folder you unpacked it to, or allow it under System Settings › Privacy & Security.

Build from source

You need Go 1.24+ and Node 20.19+.

git clone https://github.com/Xafloc/ahp-matrix && cd ahp-matrix
make run    # builds the UI and the binary, then starts it

ahp-matrix --help lists the flags (--port, --host, --data-dir, --no-open). Projects are stored in ~/Library/Application Support/ahp-matrix (macOS), %AppData%\ahp-matrix (Windows) or ~/.local/share/ahp-matrix (Linux) unless --data-dir is given. Each decision is one .ahp.json file; deleted ones move to a trash folder there.

Development

make test        # Go tests (race detector)
make lint        # gofmt + go vet
make web-check   # type-check and unit-test the UI
make e2e         # end-to-end browser tests against the real binary
make snapshot    # build release archives for every platform into dist/

Releases are cut by pushing a v* tag; .github/workflows/release.yml runs GoReleaser.

For live-reloading UI work, run the API in one terminal (make build && bin/ahp-matrix --no-open) and cd web && npm run dev in another, then open http://localhost:5173.

License

MIT
